public_rationale: The evidence establishes that substantial compute prepayments exist. CoreWeave describes them as typical across its committed customers, and Anthropic confirms historical prepaid hosting. Neither establishes how often AI labs made material advance payments during the target year alongside their ongoing expenses. The unspecified accounting basis also prevents a definitive financial score under the supplied rules.
limitations: This is an evidence gap, not a finding that prepayments were rare.
Upfront commitments and upfront cash payments must remain distinct.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI labs often must pay large up-front sums for future compute on top of very high ongoing costs.

statement.excerpt: This means that AI labs are often having to pony up massive amounts of up-front capital on top of their incredibly high ongoing costs.
statement.document_title: The Subprime AI Crisis Is Here

from_speaker: on top of their incredibly high ongoing costs
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that material cash payments before compute delivery are a recurring practice among AI labs, alongside substantial continuing operating expenses.
Use calendar 2025, the latest completed annual financial period before publication. The post gives no reporting period for this ongoing industry-wide assertion.

A commitment to future payments is not itself an upfront cash payment. Prepayments may subsequently offset service bills; the claim concerns financing demands, not necessarily additional lifetime expense.
No accounting basis or numerical threshold for materiality is specified.
criteria.support_condition: Representative contracts and payment records show that AI labs repeatedly paid material sums before receiving compute, alongside substantial ongoing expenses during the target period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative records show that material advance payments were exceptional rather than recurring, or that the asserted substantial ongoing expenses did not exist.
